data.name: ConnectingMessage
data.comment: Displayed to user in a server window when trying to connect.

data.name: CertificateRejectedMessage
data.value: Could not connect: the server's TLS certificate is not trusted.
data.comment: Displayed to the user when a TLS connection fails because the server's certificate did not pass validation, and FlamingIRC did not report the certificate.

data.name: CertificateRefusedMessage
data.value: Refused {0}: its certificate is not trusted, because {1}.
data.comment: First line of the error block for a refused certificate. {0} is host:port. {1} is one or more CertificateReason strings.

data.name: CertificateFingerprintLine
data.comment: The fingerprint line of the refused-certificate error block. {0} is colon-separated uppercase hex.

data.name: CertificateChangedMessage
data.value: WARNING: the certificate of {0} has CHANGED since you pinned it. Someone may be intercepting the connection, or the server got a new certificate.
data.comment: First line of the error block when a refused certificate is for an entry point that has a pin. {0} is host:port.

data.name: CertificatePinnedLine
data.comment: The fingerprint of the pinned certificate, in the changed-certificate error block.

data.name: CertificateNowLine
data.comment: The fingerprint of the certificate the server sent now, in the changed-certificate error block.

data.name: CertificateReasonNameMismatch
data.value: it is issued for {0}, not this host
data.comment: Reason for a refused certificate. {0} is the name the certificate is issued for.

data.name: CertificateReasonSelfSigned
data.value: it is self-signed, so no trusted authority vouches for it
data.comment: Reason for a refused certificate.

data.name: CertificateReasonExpired
data.comment: Reason for a refused certificate. {0} is the expiry date.

data.name: CertificateReasonUntrusted
data.value: no trusted authority vouches for it
data.comment: Reason for a refused certificate, for any chain error that the other reasons do not explain.

data.name: CertificateReasonSeparator
data.comment: Joins two reasons for a refused certificate.

data.name: ConnectionFailedMessage
data.comment: Displayed to the user when a connection attempt is not successful.

data.name: ConnectionFailedUnknownMessage
data.value: Could not connect: the connection failed before it was established.
data.comment: Displayed to the user when a connection attempt fails for a reason that has no socket error code, for example when the server closes the connection during the TLS handshake.

data.name: TlsHandshakeFailedMessage
data.value: Could not connect: the TLS handshake with the server failed.
data.comment: Displayed to the user when a TLS connection fails for a reason other than the server's certificate, for example when the client and the server have no TLS version in common.

data.name: RandomNickMessage
data.value: All of your alternate nicks were taken, so one was randomly chosen for you.

data.name: WarnDisconnect
data.comment: Displayed to the user when an action they performed will indirectly cause disconnection.

data.name: ConnectionLost
data.comment: Displayed to the user when a socket error ends the connection. {0} describes the socket error.

data.name: ConnectionLostServerClosed
data.comment: Displayed to the user when the server closes the connection.

data.name: ConnectionLostPingTimeout
data.comment: Displayed to the user when the client ends the connection because the server did not answer a keep-alive ping in time.

data.name: ConnectionLostUnknownMessage
data.comment: Displayed to the user when the connection ends for a reason that has no socket error code and no other wording.

data.name: StatusConnected
data.comment: Sidebar connection state for a registered connection.

data.name: StatusConnectedSecure
data.comment: Sidebar connection state for a registered connection over TLS.

data.name: StatusConnectedUnverified
data.comment: Sidebar connection state for a TLS connection that was accepted only because the network's "Verify TLS certificates" switch is off.

data.name: ConnectedUnverifiedWarning
data.value: Connected to {0}:{1} without checking its certificate. Verification is off for this network.
data.comment: Warning in the server window when a TLS connection was accepted only because verification is off. {0} is the host, {1} the port.

data.name: StatusConnecting
data.comment: Sidebar connection state while a connection attempt is in flight.

data.name: StatusReconnecting
data.comment: Sidebar connection state while waiting to reconnect. {0} is the attempt number.

data.name: StatusCertificateRefused
data.comment: Sidebar connection state after every entry point refused its certificate, so Mutiny stopped trying.

data.name: EveryEntryPointRefusedMessage
data.value: Every server refused its certificate. Mutiny stopped trying. Trust a certificate, or reconnect.
data.comment: Displayed in the server window when every entry point of the network refused its TLS certificate, so no reconnect is scheduled.

data.name: StatusDisconnected
data.comment: Sidebar connection state for a connection that is down.

data.name: StatusConnectedPinned
data.comment: Sidebar connection state for a TLS connection whose certificate failed the normal check but matches the pinned certificate.

data.name: ConnectedPinnedMessage
data.value: Connected to {0}:{1}. Its certificate failed the normal check, but it matches the one you pinned.
data.comment: Displayed in the server window when a TLS connection was accepted through a pinned certificate. {0} is the host, {1} the port.

data.name: ReconnectButton
data.comment: Button on the message that every server refused its certificate. It dials the first server of the network again.

data.name: TrustCertificateButton
data.comment: Button on a certificate refusal that pins the refused certificate and connects again.

data.name: ReplacePinnedCertificateButton
data.comment: Button on a changed-certificate refusal. It opens a confirm dialog before it replaces the pin.

data.name: CertificatePinHostOnOtherPort
data.value: Mutiny cannot pin this certificate, because a saved network lists {0} on a port other than {1}. Change the port of that entry point in the Networks dialog, then connect again.
data.comment: Displayed when the user trusts a certificate of a host that a saved network lists on a different port. {0} is the host, {1} the refused port.

data.name: ReplacePinTitle
data.comment: Title of the dialog that confirms a pin replacement.

data.name: ReplacePinMessage
data.value: The certificate of {0}:{1} is not the one you pinned. Someone may be intercepting the connection. Replace the pin only if you know that the server got a new certificate.
data.comment: Text of the dialog that confirms a pin replacement. {0} is the host, {1} the port.

data.name: ReplacePinConfirmButton
data.comment: Button in the pin replacement dialog that replaces the pin.

data.name: ReplacePinCancelButton
data.comment: Button in the pin replacement dialog that keeps the old pin.

data.name: VerifyCertificatesOnHint
data.value: Refuses a server whose certificate fails the check, unless you pinned that certificate
data.comment: Networks dialog: the hint under the "Verify TLS certificates" switch when the switch is on.

data.name: VerifyCertificatesOffHint
data.value: Off: Mutiny accepts any certificate from this network's servers
data.comment: Networks dialog: the warning under the "Verify TLS certificates" switch when the switch is off.

data.name: VerifyCertificatesNoTlsHint
data.value: None of this network's servers use TLS, so there is no certificate to check.
data.comment: Networks dialog: the hint under the "Verify TLS certificates" switch when no entry point of the network uses TLS.

data.name: EntryPointPinLine
data.comment: Networks dialog: the line under a pinned entry point. {0} is the first bytes of the pinned fingerprint.
